title: Transport of left proper combinatorial simplicial models along equivalences
statement:
Use model categories, left properness, combinatoriality, simplicial enrichment, tensor, cotensor and pushout products in the conventions of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], with simplicial sets and Kan weak equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $E:\mathcal C\simeq\mathcal D$ be an equivalence of ordinary categories with a chosen quasi-inverse $G$, and let $\mathcal D$ have a left proper combinatorial model structure. Give $\mathcal C$ the three classes obtained by inverse image under $E$ of the cofibrations, fibrations and weak equivalences of $\mathcal D$. These classes form a left proper combinatorial model structure. Fibrant and cofibrant objects are detected by $E$. If $I,J$ generate the two weak factorization systems in $\mathcal D$, then $G(I),G(J)$ generate those in $\mathcal C$; local presentability is preserved under $E$. The model factorizations can be chosen functorially using $E,G$ and their unit and counit.

Suppose additionally that $\mathcal D$ is simplicial, that $\mathcal C$ has specified enrichment $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}$, tensors and cotensors, and that $R:\mathrm{sSet}\simeq\mathrm{sSet}$ is a strong cartesian monoidal equivalence preserving and reflecting Kan cofibrations and weak equivalences. Assume coherent natural isomorphisms
$$E(X\otimes K)\cong EX\otimes RK,\qquad E(Y^K)\cong(EY)^{RK},\qquad\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(X,Y)\cong R^{-1}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(EX,EY),$$
respecting the tensor-cotensor adjunctions, units and enriched composition. Then the specified enrichment makes the transported model structure simplicial: its pushout-product axiom is detected under $E$. The conclusion includes the identity choice of $R$ and the simplicial order-reversal involution of [lem-coef-simplicial-opposite-homotopy-calculus]. Finally an adjunction between two categories transported in this fashion is Quillen whenever, under the equivalences, it identifies with a Quillen adjunction between their given model categories.

source.place: HTT Section 3.1.3, opposite convention, abstract model-transport argument extracted from former Step 14. Basic transport is Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology/ModelCategory/Transport.lean:39-76; the left proper, generating-set and twisted simplicial clauses are the additional argument. No Stacks tag; HTT unavailable in literature/.

proof.text: Apply the finite model-axiom transport lemma to $E$ and the three inverse-image classes. Its hypotheses hold for the given model category $\mathcal D$: the two weak factorization systems give the lifting and factorization axioms, and their classes are retract closed. Thus two-out-of-three, retract closure, both lifting assertions and both kinds of factorization hold in $\mathcal C$. These assertions also identify the two weak factorization systems: for example, factor an arrow lifting against every trivial fibration as $pi$ with $i$ a cofibration and $p$ a trivial fibration; the lift against $p$ makes the arrow a retract of $i$. The reverse inclusion is the lifting axiom. The identical retract argument with the other factorization treats the other three lifting classes.

source.place: ModelCategory.transport:39-71; retract characterization of the two lifting classes

proof.text: Use the natural Hom bijections for the quasi-inverse adjunctions $E\dashv G$ and $G\dashv E$. If $H:I\to\mathcal C$ is any small diagram, put $L=\lim_I EH$ and $Q=\operatorname{colim}_I EH$, which exist by completeness and cocompleteness of $\mathcal D$. For every $X$, the bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,GL)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(EX,L)$ identifies maps with cones from $EX$ to $EH$ and hence, by full faithfulness of $E$, with cones from $X$ to $H$. Dually $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(GQ,X)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(Q,EX)$ identifies maps with cocones from $H$ to $X$. Therefore $GL$ and $GQ$ supply all small limits and colimits in $\mathcal C$. This also includes the empty diagram.

source.place: Tags 001J (definition-equivalence-categories), 0037 (definition-adjoint); direct cone and cocone universal properties

proof.text:
Choose the adjoint-equivalence unit $\eta:1_{\mathcal C}\cong GE$ and counit $\varepsilon:EG\cong1_{\mathcal D}$. For either given functorial factorization $Ef=p_f i_f$ through $Z_f$, define the factorization of $f:X\to Y$ by
$$X\xrightarrow{G(i_f)\eta_X}GZ_f\xrightarrow{\eta_Y^{-1}G(p_f)}Y.$$
Naturality of $\eta$ makes the composite $\eta_Y^{-1}GE(f)\eta_X=f$. The triangle identity gives $E\eta_X=\varepsilon_{EX}^{-1}$; naturality of $\varepsilon$ then identifies the two image arrows with $\varepsilon_{Z_f}^{-1}i_f$ and $p_f\varepsilon_{Z_f}$. Their classes are those of $i_f,p_f$, since an isomorphism of arrows exhibits each arrow as a retract of the other and the classes are retract closed. A square from $f$ to $f'$ is sent to the chosen middle map $Z_f\to Z_{f'}$ and then by $G$ to $GZ_f\to GZ_{f'}$; naturality of $\eta$ gives both required squares. Identity and composition follow from functoriality in $\mathcal D$ and of $G$. Thus both factorizations in $\mathcal C$ are functorial.

source.place: Quasi-inverse adjunctions, Tags 001J and 0037; explicit functorial factorization formula supplementing Mathlib transport

proof.text: Equivalences preserve initial and terminal objects, as the empty colimit and empty limit. Consequently $E(\varnothing_{\mathcal C}\to X)$ and $E(X\to1_{\mathcal C})$ identify, up to isomorphism of arrows, with $\varnothing_{\mathcal D}\to EX$ and $EX\to1_{\mathcal D}$. By the inverse-image definitions and isomorphism invariance from Step 3, $X$ is cofibrant exactly when $EX$ is cofibrant, and fibrant exactly when $EX$ is fibrant.

source.place: Tag 0038 (lemma-adjoint-exact), empty diagrams; definitions of fibrant and cofibrant

proof.text: For $i:A\to B$ in $\mathcal D$ and $p:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal C$, the adjunction $G\dashv E$ sends a square $(a:GA\to X,b:GB\to Y)$ to its two adjoints $(\bar a:A\to EX,\bar b:B\to EY)$. Naturality says $pa=bG(i)$ exactly when $(Ep)\bar a=\bar b i$, and a filler $d:GB\to X$ corresponds to $\bar d:B\to EX$ with precisely the two filler equations. Thus $G(i)$ lifts against $p$ if and only if $i$ lifts against $Ep$. Applying this to every $i\in I$ gives $(G I)^{\perp}=E^{-1}(I^{\perp})$, the trivial fibrations of $\mathcal C$; applying it to every $j\in J$ gives $(G J)^{\perp}$ equal to the fibrations of $\mathcal C$. The left classes are uniquely determined by the right classes in a weak factorization system (Step 1). Hence $G(I),G(J)$ generate the two transported systems. They are sets because they are images of the given sets.

source.place: Tag 0037 (definition-adjoint), naturality of the Hom bijection; direct generator test

proof.text: Apply invariance of local presentability to $E$ (in the direction from $\mathcal D$ to $\mathcal C$). Together with the two generating sets of Step 5, this proves combinatoriality in the stated convention.

Left properness means that pushing out a weak equivalence along a cofibration gives a weak equivalence. Let $w:A\to B$ be a weak equivalence and $i:A\to A'$ a cofibration of $\mathcal C$. Equivalence preservation of colimits makes the image of the pushout square a pushout square in $\mathcal D$. Its initial arrows are $Ew$ and $Ei$, a weak equivalence and a cofibration by definition. Left properness in $\mathcal D$ makes the resulting map $EA'\to E(B\amalg_A A')$ a weak equivalence. Reflection by the inverse-image class proves the assertion in $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Tag 0038 (lemma-adjoint-exact); direct application of the given left properness

proof.text:
Let $i:A\to B$ be a morphism in $\mathcal C$ and $j:K\to L$ a simplicial map. The pushout product has source $(B\otimes K)\amalg_{A\otimes K}(A\otimes L)$ and target $B\otimes L$. Apply $E$. Preservation of the pushout and the assumed tensor comparisons identify its source with $(EB\otimes RK)\amalg_{EA\otimes RK}(EA\otimes RL)$ and its target with $EB\otimes RL$. Naturality of the tensor comparisons identifies the two legs and the two maps into the target with those induced by $Ei$ and $Rj$. The universal property therefore identifies the entire arrow, not just its endpoints:
$$E(i\mathbin\square j)\cong(Ei)\mathbin\square(Rj).$$

source.place: Tag 0038 (lemma-adjoint-exact), applied to the pushout-product cocone; direct tensor comparison

proof.text: If $i,j$ are cofibrations, $Ei$ and $Rj$ are cofibrations. The simplicial axiom in the given category $\mathcal D$ makes $(Ei)\mathbin\square(Rj)$ a cofibration. It is trivial if $i$ is trivial (since $Ei$ is then trivial), or if $j$ is trivial (since $R$ preserves Kan weak equivalences). Step 8 and the inverse-image classes give exactly the same conclusions for $i\mathbin\square j$ in $\mathcal C$. The specified enrichment, tensors and cotensors already satisfy the enriched composition and tensor-cotensor adjunctions by the coherence assumptions. Thus the only additional model condition is this pushout-product axiom, which has just been checked by applying $E$. No independent enrichment is substituted for the specified one.

source.place: Paragraph 2, finite-coefficient mapping-complex adjunction: abstract simplicial transport deduction below the relative marked model

proof.text: The identity parameter equivalence satisfies the required conditions. For order reversal, the current opposite-calculus statement gives a covariant involution and states that opposite preserves and reflects Kan complexes and Kan fibrations; its degreewise action gives $(K\times L)^{\mathrm{op}}=K^{\mathrm{op}}\times L^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $(\Delta^0)^{\mathrm{op}}=\Delta^0$. The cartesian comparison maps are identities on components, so their associativity, symmetry and unit diagrams commute. Kan cofibrations are degreewise injections, which are unchanged by reversal. The existing opposite-subdivision lemma supplies preservation and reflection of weak homotopy equivalences via the natural barycentric-coordinate homeomorphism of realizations. Therefore this strong cartesian monoidal involution meets the hypotheses on $R$, and Steps 8–9 apply whenever the specified enrichment comparisons in the statement are supplied.

source.place: Paragraph 2, finite mapping-complex adjunction: order-reversal convention; existing opposite and realization comparison statements

proof.text: Finally write the transported adjunction as $L:\mathcal C_1\rightleftarrows\mathcal C_2:U$ and the given Quillen adjunction as $L':\mathcal D_1\rightleftarrows\mathcal D_2:U'$. The assumed identification under the equivalences includes a natural isomorphism $E_2L\cong L'E_1$. For a cofibration $i$ in $\mathcal C_1$, the arrow $E_1i$ is a cofibration; hence $L'E_1i$ is one, and so is $E_2Li$. If $i$ is also a weak equivalence, $L'E_1i$ and $E_2Li$ are trivial cofibrations instead. Reflection by $E_2$ proves that $L$ preserves both cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. This is precisely the left-adjoint definition of a Quillen adjunction; the ordinary adjunction is already a hypothesis.

source.place: Paragraph 2, finite mapping-complex adjunction: direct check of the Quillen condition under the assumed identification
